NOTIFY-001.summary: Extend requester updates to public replies and approved comments while retaining consent and customer-safe visibility.
NOTIFY-001.was: A follower receives published request status updates, declines, and mapped roadmap status updates subject to mute and suppression; republishing a version sends nothing again.
NOTIFY-001.now: Followers receive only customer-safe published status updates, declines, mapped roadmap status updates, public operator replies and approved requester comments, subject to current visibility, consent, mute and suppression; held comments and internal notes send nothing.

NOTIFY-002.summary: Define the fixed first-event one-minute coalescing window, Queue wakeups at publication and the minute-Cron backstop.
NOTIFY-002.was: One-click unsubscribe and request/all-email mute are checked before send; default quiet hours are 20:00–08:00 workspace time and updates within one hour are coalesced.
NOTIFY-002.now: The first pending event opens a fixed one-minute requester/request coalescing window; later events never extend it. Publication wakes a Queue consumer that sends eligible windows after the boundary and outside 20:00–08:00 workspace quiet hours, rechecking visibility and preferences immediately before sending; the minute Cron is the backstop for a failed Queue handoff. An optional validated WORKSPACE_TIMEZONE deployment input selects the IANA workspace timezone before setup. Published release versions use independent recipient commands outside request coalescing and wait for earlier request updates to settle.

REL-006.summary: Retain ambiguous SendGrid outcomes as unknown without automatic retry.
REL-006.was: Unknown sends retried under a provider idempotency key.
REL-006.now: SendGrid lacks provider duplicate suppression; ambiguous/interrupted sends remain unknown and are never automatically retried. REL-007 provider-idempotency remains unsatisfied; local claims and delivery correlation are not an exactly-once provider guarantee. Status, reply, approved-comment and release publications enqueue a wakeup on the JOBS Queue; the consumer drains due notification windows and release recipient commands with bounded retry for known refusals and rate limits, and holds ambiguous sends as unknown. Hosted installs must declare the JOBS queue consumer (deploy.json, wrangler.jsonc); the minute Cron remains the recovery path.

BASE-SECRET-002.summary: Allow deployed public reading and already verified requester actions before mail is configured.
BASE-SECRET-002.was: Mail provider and sender are required deployment inputs.
BASE-SECRET-002.now: Both mail provider and sender may be absent together. New emailed sign-in and verification explain that delivery is unavailable. Existing verified native sessions and valid host assertions for a stored verified address may submit; an already delivered verification link can complete once and replay its bound pending actions. First-time host provisioning and anonymous holds retain the transport admission boundary. Partial or invalid mail configuration still fails. MAIL_PROVIDER, MAIL_FROM, MAIL_API_KEY and MAIL_RELAY_URL are deploy.json secrets read from the deploy environment; rer deploy accepts sendgrid, resend or rer and refuses a deployment without sign-in email. Local copies send no email; operators add verified test customers in Penny Dev instead of reading an outbox.

DATA-001.summary: Enable authenticated hosted product archive and erasure-journal downloads with explicit custody bounds.
DATA-001.was: Archive downloads were limited to local/test installations.
DATA-001.now: Current native operators may download the bounded classified product archive and latest erasure journal over authenticated HTTPS. Original R2 bytes retain hashes; unknown schema, missing files and overflow refuse completion. Guarded restore and erasure now use current native authority, same-origin mutation, maintenance, empty-target, latest-known-journal and preview-hash fences in hosted mode as well as local/test. Hosted proof is source-only, local TLS; a real installation and universal data acceptance remain owner/live and open. Hosted Data → Export keeps partial and completed snapshots across reloads, offers resume and releases the snapshot with Finish export.
